items.title: Framer Updates: Image and Shader Generation
items.excerpt: The Framer Agent can now generate or edit images, textures and illustrations and create or tweak shaders such as halftone, bokeh or CRT. It can also feed a generated image into an image shader.
items.rationale: Primary-source release: Framer's agent now generates images and shaders on the site canvas, so designers can make visual assets without leaving the site builder. Picked over the duplicate Framer YouTube demo (cluster c2).

items.title: 5 new Google Flow Tools designed by visual artists
items.excerpt: Google added five creative tools to Flow, its AI filmmaking studio, built with visual artists: they keep characters consistent across decades, generate stylized art, simulate complex lighting and turn phone videos into polished shots.
items.rationale: New tools from the primary source covering character consistency, stylization, lighting simulation and phone-to-polished shots, all directly usable in visual production.

items.title: KT, 앱 디자인부터 고객 안내 문구까지 AI 적용…'KDS 2.0' 구축
items.excerpt: KT built KDS 2.0, a UX design system that AI can read directly. Its 'KDS Harness' lets AI lay out screens to the system's rules and check the results, cutting about 8 months of work (424 requirements, 25 components) to 2 months 40 days. KT also launched an AI message-writing agent that cuts drafting and review from 30-60 minutes to about 5.
items.rationale: A concrete enterprise case of an AI-readable design system plus a harness that checks generated screens against it, with measured time savings that design-system teams can benchmark against.

items.title: Rhino World 2026: McNeel lets AI in
items.excerpt: With Rhino 9 out, AEC Magazine reports from Rhino World 2026 on how McNeel is bringing AI into Rhino and speeding up development without changing its perpetual-licence business model.
items.rationale: McNeel opening Rhino to AI is a direction change for a core tool used by product, industrial and architectural designers. Reported from the event by a specialist outlet.

items.title: Should You Actually Add AI To That? A Four-Question Audit For Product Teams
items.excerpt: An AI feature can save users time on a task, then cost them that time checking its output. Smashing offers a four-question audit for deciding where AI earns its place in a product and what users need to trust it.
items.rationale: A practical framework a product designer can use in tomorrow's roadmap review, from a whitelisted, reputable outlet. It uses a second tokens slot, so it gets a distinct palette accent.
